# Checking that the contributor rules cite real locations

The project's contributor rules live in the tracked source tree, so every
checkout carries the copy a contributor reads. Every path they cite resolves,
and a curated set of known-dead references stays out.

## Resolve what the rules cite

Read `.claude/rules/rules.md`, take every backtick-quoted token in a
filesystem-path shape, and stat each against the repository root.

The shape rule this project recognises: drop a leading `./`; reject URLs,
`make …` invocations, and tokens carrying `*` or `{`; accept a trailing `/`;
otherwise require a repository file extension, and either a `/` or a root-level
filename shape. Drop the Search Scoping line, which lists paths to exclude from
searches rather than paths to read.

At this release ten cited paths are in scope and all ten resolve:

```
lib/services/test/
CLAUDE.md
tools/gotest-guard.sh
lib/protocols/proto/v1/events.proto
.golangci.yml
./CLAUDE.md
.ok-planner/sketches/
.ok-planner/issues/
.ok-planner/workbench/
.claude/rules/citation-grammar.md
```

The population is non-empty, so the check has something to be wrong about rather
than passing vacuously.

## Check the build steps the rules name

All four make targets the rules name are declared in the Makefile:

```
core-images
lint
proto-gen
service-images
```

The rules name `make core-images` as the image-rebuild step the verification
sequence depends on.

## Keep dead references out

A curated set of four references known to be dead must not appear in the rules:

```
deploy/build-images.sh
deploy/docker-compose.yml
executors/claude-agent
docs/2026-04-25-stores-redesign.md
```

None of the four appears at this release. That is the ratchet: a reference
removed once does not creep back in unnoticed as the rules are edited.

## Confirm the file is the one contributors get

```bash
git ls-files --error-unmatch .claude/rules/rules.md
```

The rules file is tracked, so every contributor's checkout carries the file that
was measured.
